Purpose The aim of the study was to investigate the effect of a 6-week, low-dose bovine colostrum (BC) supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) and performance decline in soccer players following the Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) during a competitive season period. Methods In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled design, two groups of soccer players were allocated to a 3.2 g/day of whey protein (WP, N = 8) or BC ( N = 10) and performed a pre- and a post-supplementation LIST. Maximum isometric voluntary contraction, squat jump (SQJ), countermovement jump, muscle soreness, blood cell counts, creatine kinase (CK), C-reactive protein (CRP) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) were monitored for 2, 24, 48, 72 h post-LIST. Results LIST induced transient increases in leukocytes, granulocytes, CK, muscle soreness, CRP, IL-6 and declines in lymphocytes and performance indices. Supplementation resulted in a faster recovery of SQJ, CK and CRP compared to pre-supplementation kinetics (trial × time: p = 0.001, 0.056, 0.014, respectively) and lower incremental area under the curve (iAUC) for IL-6, only in the BC group [pre-: 31.1 (6.78–46.9), post-: 14.0 (−0.16 to 23.5) pg h/ml, p = 0.034]. Direct comparison of the two groups after supplementation demonstrated higher iAUC of SQJ [WP: −195.2 (−229.0 to (−52.5)), BC: −15.8 (−93.2 to 16.8) cm h, p = 0.034], a trend for lower iAUC of CK in the BC group [WP: 18,785 (4651–41,357), BC: 8842 (4807–14,802) U h/L, p = 0.081] and a significant intervention × time interaction for CRP ( p = 0.038) in favor of BC. Conclusions Post-exercise EIMD may be reduced and performance better maintained by a low dose of BC administration following LIST in soccer players. Keywords Bovine colostrum Exercise-induced muscle damage Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test Soccer Inflammation Squat jump LR Health and Beauty Systems issue-copyright-statement © Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2018 Introduction Elite-level soccer games are characterized by high-intensity intermittent physical activity. The repetitive and eccentric nature of soccer movements (accelerations, decelerations, kicking, jumping, and tackling) can cause muscle damage, accompanied by the leakage of muscle enzymes and other functional proteins in the circulation, oxidative stress, inflammation and decline in muscle performance [ 1 , 2 ]. The clinical phenotype of post-match muscle damage can strongly impair the recovery process [ 3 ]. Taking into account the congested schedule of elite soccer players (2 or even 3 matches per week) the recovery period is not optimal for the restoration of pre-match exercise capacity and performance, while it may increase the risk for muscle injuries [ 4 ]. Since the extent of muscle damage can determine the duration of the recovery period, several strategies, aiming to attenuate muscle damage and accelerate the recovery period, are under research. However, the majority is adopting physiotherapeutic and training modalities like stretching, cryotherapy, active recovery, sleeping, massage, electrical stimulation and compression garments [ 5 ], while the nutritional or supplementation interventions are much less studied under real post-soccer match conditions. Interventions including the administration of creatine [ 6 ], antioxidant vitamins [ 7 , 8 ], astaxanthin [ 9 ], beta-alanine [ 10 ], omega-3 fatty acids [ 11 ] are tested for their ability to reduce exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) or to increase exercise performance after a soccer match or a simulation of a soccer match. However, the results so far are inconclusive concerning the ability of supplements to improve the recovery process [ 5 ]. Bovine colostrum (BC) is the first milk produced by the mammary glands of the mother during the final days of pregnancy and the first days postpartum (1–4 days). It is as rich in carbohydrates, proteins, fats and micro-nutrients (minerals, trace elements) as the regular milk, but it additionally contains high amounts of oligosaccharides, growth factors, antimicrobial agents and immunoregulatory compounds [ 12 ]. It is therefore a natural multi-ingredient supplement with potential pleiotropic properties. Previous studies focused, mainly, on its effect on exercise performance, body composition [ 13 ], immune system and its ability to counteract upper respiratory tract infections [ 14 ]. However, the doses of BC in these studies were relatively high (20–60 g/day). So far, the ability of BC to enhance the recovery after a high-intensity soccer match is implied only indirectly through its anabolic properties [ 15 ], its buffering capacity [ 16 ] and its ability to attenuate post-exercise intestinal permeability [ 17 ] and oxidative stress [ 18 ]. In order to shed more light on this issue, aim of the present study was to investigate the effect of a low-dose BC supplementation on EIMD and performance in soccer players, during their competitive season, following the Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) which simulates the activity pattern of a real soccer match [ 19 ].

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 6-week, low-dose bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), inflammatory indices, hematological markers, and performance decline in soccer players following a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST). The LIST protocol induced transient changes in immune cells, inflammatory markers, and declines in performance. BC supplementation demonstrated potential in mitigating some EIMD, improving recovery of muscle power (SQJ), and attenuating post-exercise increases in inflammatory markers (CRP, CK, IL-6) compared to pre-supplementation and/or whey protein, suggesting better maintenance of performance and reduced post-exercise EIMD.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Bovine Colostrum (BC) and Whey Protein (WP) supplementation in conjunction with a Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: A low-dose of 3.2 g/day of either bovine colostrum (BC) or whey protein (WP) was administered for 6 weeks to soccer players. This consisted of 8 capsules x 400 mg per capsule. The LIST protocol was performed pre- and post-supplementation. No dose-response comparisons for the supplements were reported, as only one dose was used; however, comparisons were made between pre- and post-supplementation responses, and directly between the BC and WP groups.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially lower after LIST (7–9% decline at 24–48h post-LIST 1), but BC supplementation led to a faster recovery compared to pre-supplementation kinetics (trial × time: p = 0.001) and significantly higher iAUC in the BC group compared to WP [WP: -195.2 (-229.0 to -52.5) cm h, BC: -15.8 (-93.2 to 16.8) cm h, p = 0.034]. BC attenuated the decline in performance and improved recovery of SQJ.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Assessment of lower limb explosive power and muscle function, measuring lower body explosive power and muscle elastic capabilities.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) recovery in soccer players following 6-week low-dose bovine colostrum supplementation, with comparison to whey protein.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates maintained or improved athletic performance, muscle recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), and improved recovery of muscle power.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (3- to 4-fold increase, peaked at 24-48h) after LIST. BC supplementation resulted in a faster recovery compared to pre-supplementation kinetics (trial × time: p = 0.056) and a trend for lower iAUC in the BC group compared to WP [WP: 18,785 (4651–41,357) U h/L, BC: 8842 (4807–14,802) U h/L, p = 0.081]. Lower elevations were statistically significant 24h after LIST in the BC group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enzyme released from damaged muscle cells into circulation, serving as a primary indicator of muscle cell damage and integrity loss.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Monitored for 72 hours post-Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) to assess exercise-induced muscle damage and the effects of 6-week low-dose bovine colostrum supplementation, comparing pre- and post-supplementation and against whey protein.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a primary indicator of exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD). Lower levels or faster recovery suggest reduced muscle damage and potential mitigation of EIMD.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (fivefold, peaked at 24-48h) after LIST. BC supplementation resulted in a faster recovery compared to pre-supplementation kinetics (trial × time: p = 0.014). Lower CRP values were observed at 72h after LIST 2 compared to LIST 1 in the BC group, with a significant intervention × time interaction (p = 0.038) and significant differences in % changes between BC LIST 1 and BC LIST 2 (p=0.038) and between WP LIST 2 and BC LIST 2 (p=0.031) in favor of BC.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Acute phase protein, systemic marker of inflammation synthesized by the liver, which increases in response to inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) recovery in soccer players following 6-week low-dose bovine colostrum supplementation, comparing pre- and post-supplementation and against whey protein.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammatory response to exercise-induced stress. Lower levels or faster recovery suggest attenuated inflammation and reduced systemic inflammation following exercise-induced muscle damage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (fourfold peak at 2h, returning to basal levels at 24h) after LIST. BC supplementation led to significantly lower incremental area under the curve (iAUC) for IL-6 (pre-: 31.1 (6.78–46.9) pg h/ml, post-: 14.0 (−0.16 to 23.5) pg h/ml, p = 0.034) and significantly lower increments (p = 0.028) in LIST 2 compared to LIST 1 in the BC group [LIST 1: 351% (243–601%); LIST 2: 254% (178–339%)].

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in the acute phase response, inflammation, immune regulation, muscle regeneration, and energy metabolism.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST) recovery in soccer players, specifically within the bovine colostrum supplementation group, assessing inflammatory and immune responses related to exercise-induced muscle damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects the magnitude of inflammatory response and muscle damage. Lower iAUC indicates attenuated inflammation and modulated immune response after intense exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (transient, twofold increase 2h post-LIST 1, returned to baseline at 24h) after LIST. BC supplementation did not significantly affect leukocyte counts compared to pre-supplementation or WP group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: White blood cells, crucial for immune defense and inflammatory processes, component of the immune system.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise. BC supplementation was evaluated for its effect on these counts.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an immediate immunological and inflammatory response to strenuous exercise; BC did not significantly modulate the overall count.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (transient, approximately 2.5-fold increase 2h post-LIST 1). BC supplementation did not significantly affect granulocyte counts compared to pre-supplementation or WP group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell, primarily involved in innate immune responses, particularly against infections and inflammation, mediating inflammation and fighting infection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise. BC supplementation was evaluated for its effect on these counts.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an immediate immune system activation and inflammatory response to strenuous exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially lower (significant 30% decline 2h post-LIST 1). While BC supplementation did not prevent the initial decline, a higher iAUC for lymphocytes (p = 0.017) was observed in the BC group compared to the WP group after LIST 2.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A type of white blood cell crucial for adaptive immunity, involved in specific immune responses and immune surveillance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise, and post-supplementation comparison between WP and BC.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a transient shift in immune cell distribution or acute immune suppression/modulation post-exercise. Higher iAUC in BC group suggests altered lymphocyte response post-supplementation, potentially linked to immune function.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially higher (significant increase evident at 24–48 h post-LIST 1, more pronounced in knee extensors and flexors). BC supplementation did not significantly affect perceived muscle soreness, though WP showed lower VAS for knee flexors post-LIST 2.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Subjective perception of pain or discomfort in muscles, typically resulting from exercise-induced muscle damage, often associated with delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise. BC supplementation was evaluated for its effect on muscle soreness.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a subjective indicator of muscle damage and fatigue, impacting recovery and subsequent performance. BC did not significantly alleviate it in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially lower (sustained significant decline of ~8 to 10% from 2 to 48 h post-LIST). BC supplementation did not significantly affect MIVC kinetics, with similar declines observed for LIST 1 and LIST 2 in both groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures maximal muscle strength without changes in muscle length, assessing maximal muscle strength output.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute muscle fatigue and strength loss following strenuous exercise; BC did not significantly improve it in this study.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Initially lower (sustained significant decline of ~8 to 10% from 24 to 48 h post-LIST). BC supplementation did not significantly affect CMJ kinetics, with similar declines observed for LIST 1 and LIST 2 in both groups. The stretch-shortening cycle in CMJ might mask negative performance effects.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures lower body explosive power and reactive strength, incorporating eccentric-concentric muscle actions.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Acute response immediately following Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test (LIST), and post-supplementation LIST 2 exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates acute muscle fatigue and decline in athletic performance following strenuous exercise; BC did not significantly improve it in this study, potentially due to methodological factors masking effects.
